Trend: Day -6 to -4 rest HR 70-72, sleep 6.9-7.2 h, bed-sensor exits 0-1 per night, steps 3000-3300; Day -2 to 0 rest HR 76-84 (84 on Day 0), sleep 5.1-5.4 h, bed-sensor exits 3-4 per night, steps 2100 on Day -2 and 1800 on Day 0. cases.rationale: Tramadol started on Day -3 on top of long-standing sertraline is followed by resting HR rising from 70-72 to 84 bpm, sleep falling to 5.1-5.4 h, bed-sensor exits rising to 3-4 a night, and a spouse report of hand shaking, night sweats and dusk confusion. Together these suggest a serotonergic or delirium-type effect that needs same-day prescriber review, but no hard rule fires: there is no SpO2, chest pain, syncope or focal finding. Provider_task fits the need for a same-business-day medication review. Naive-model trap: a shallow model reads a routine new analgesic and a mild HR rise and sends nurse_task for a routine side-effect call, missing that two serotonergic agents with new sweating, shaking and confusion need a prescriber decision today.
cases.decisive_feature: Tramadol started Day -3 on long-standing sertraline, with resting HR 84 bpm, sleep 5.1-5.4 h and spouse-reported hand shaking and night sweats.
